In assets/revamp.js add const LS_SUMMON = 'pokechest.summons.v1' storing { [pcId]: { slices:[6 PNG dataURLs], headband:dataURL, mode:'mint'|'damaged'|'psa10', palette:[hex...], created:'YYYY-MM-DD' } }, and async function spiritBuild(c): load c.img into an Image whose src is '/api/imgproxy?url='+encodeURIComponent(c.img) when c.img starts with 'http' (else c.img as-is), draw to a 96x128 canvas, getImageData; compute a 6-color palette by 4-bit RGB bucket counts (skip near-white avg>240); build a foreground mask (pixels farther than RGB distance 40 from the most common corner color), downsample the mask to a 24x32 cell grid (a cell is 'on' when more than half of its 4x4 source pixels are masked foreground). For layers l=0..5: erode the on-cell grid l times (a cell survives one erosion pass only if all 4-neighbors are on). Paint each surviving cell onto that layer's own 96x128 canvas as a filled 4x4-px rect at (cellX*4, cellY*4). Cell color, exactly: base = the per-channel arithmetic mean RGB of the foreground-masked source pixels inside the cell's 4x4 region (if none, use the palette's most frequent color); lightened for layer l as each channel ch → Math.round(ch + (255 - ch) * 0.06 * l) (i.e. moved 6%·l of the way to white). items.title: Encrypted backup export/import (then iCloud autosave)
items.spec: Phase 1, all in assets/app.js Admin tab (renderAdmin, app.js:2102): add a 'Backup & Restore' panel. backupCollect() returns {app:'pokechest', version:APP_VERSION, exported:ISO-8601, ls:{...}} where ls holds every localStorage key starting with 'pokechest.' (snapshots, userdata, den, sales, customcards, case, pregrade, arcade, etc.) with raw string values. Add async backupEncrypt(passphrase) → Uint8Array: derive an AES-GCM-256 key via PBKDF2-SHA256 (250000 iterations, random 16-byte salt) using crypto.subtle, encrypt the UTF-8 JSON of backupCollect() with a random 12-byte IV, and return the concatenation ASCII magic 'PKDEN1' + salt + iv + ciphertext. backupExport(passphrase): download await backupEncrypt(passphrase) as a Blob, filename den-backup-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pkdenbak. backupImport(file, passphrase): parse the same layout, decrypt, validate payload.app==='pokechest', show a confirm listing key count and export date, then write every ls entry back via localStorage.setItem and location.reload(). Wrong passphrase (AES-GCM auth failure) must toast a clear error and change nothing. Phase 2 (autosave): new LS key `'pokechest.backupauto.v1'` = `{enabled:boolean, pass:string, lastRun:'YYYY-MM-DD'|null}` — the passphrase is stored locally in plaintext by design (documented in the panel copy: 'the passphrase protects the backup file if it leaves this computer; it is stored on this computer'). Admin panel UI for it: an autosave checkbox, a passphrase input (writes .pass), and a folder-path input that POSTs {backup_dir:'<path>'} to the existing /api/config endpoint. Server side: add 'backup_dir' to server.py save_settings' known-keys tuple (line ~52); add POST /api/backup/save to do_POST accepting {filename, dataB64}, decoding and atomically writing to settings backup_dir if set else HOME/backups/ (os.makedirs, reject filenames containing '/' or '..'), returning {ok, path}. Client: add async backupAutosave(): read the LS record; return unless enabled && pass && State.live && (lastRun == null || (Date.now() - Date.parse(lastRun)) >= 7*86400000); const bytes = await backupEncrypt(rec.pass); base64-encode via btoa(String.fromCharCode(...)) applied in 0x8000-byte chunks; POST /api/backup/save with {filename:'den-autobackup-<YYYY-MM-DD>.pkdenbak', dataB64}; on {ok:true} set lastRun = today and save the LS record; all failures silent except a single toast on HTTP error. Call backupAutosave() once at the end of init() in app.js (after updateLiveBtn()). Pointing backup_dir at ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/<AppName>/ gives iCloud sync with no backend.

items.title: Token-smart global search
items.spec: The topbar #search / Collection filter (applyFilters() in assets/app.js) matches token-AND instead of raw substring: the query is split on whitespace and EVERY token must appear somewhere in a haystack of name + set + number + setRaw + game + language words ('japanese jp' / 'english en') + graded words (grader, grade, 'graded slab' / 'raw'). items.title: Server hardening: static blocklist, security headers, loopback-only admin
items.spec: server.py Handler: _static_blocked(path) refuses settings.local.json(.tmp), lan-tls/ (TLS private key), any *.xlsx, and every dot-path (.git/, .github/, .DS_Store) with 403 before SimpleHTTPRequestHandler sees the request — previously GET /.git/config and GET /settings.local.json (BYOK keys, when POKECHEST_HOME is unset so HOME==ROOT) were servable, including to LAN peers in phone mode. end_headers() override stamps X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on every response (static + JSON; app uses no iframes). _read_body() raises PayloadTooLarge above BODY_MAX=48MB -> 413 before reading (largest legit payload, a 25MB xlsx import as base64, is ~34MB). _loopback_only() gates admin surfaces on client_address[0] in (127.0.0.1, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1): GET/POST /api/secrets* (Keychain), /api/emerald/* (subprocess runners), any */reveal (Finder), POST /api/config (key writes), POST /api/lan (kill switch), /api/import, /api/mobile/deliver. Phone (LAN listener) keeps: app UI, /data/*, /card-art/*, /listing-photos/*, /api/health|lan(GET)|config(GET, masked)|listingphoto(s)|ai/identify|pc/*|refresh|saveimg|cardart(GET/POST).

items.title: Server-side PriceCharting search cache
items.spec: server.py: SEARCH_CACHE_FILE = HOME/search-cache.json, keyed by _search_cache_key(q) (normalized whitespace+case). search_cache_get(q) -> (products, stale) where stale=True once an entry passes SEARCH_CACHE_PRICE_TTL (6h); search_cache_put(q, products) writes with ts+lastUsed and LRU-evicts down to SEARCH_CACHE_MAX (400) by lastUsed when over cap. pc_search(q, token) checks the cache first (fresh hit -> zero network calls), on a stale/miss hits PriceCharting live and reseeds the cache, and on ANY network exception falls back to a stale cache entry if one exists (still ok:True, stale:True) rather than erroring the whole search mid-scan. Gitignored (search-cache.json) — it's regenerated data, not source.
items.ux: Invisible speedup: repeat/similar catalog searches during a scan session (Scanner + Add & Sold) return instantly instead of re-hitting PriceCharting, and a flaky connection mid-scan degrades to slightly-stale results instead of a hard failure.
acceptance: A fresh cache hit for a previously-searched query returns without calling http_json (network) at all.
An entry older than SEARCH_CACHE_PRICE_TTL reports stale=True but still returns its products.
On a live network failure with a stale cache entry present, pc_search still returns ok:True with the stale products instead of raising.
On a true cache miss with a live network failure, pc_search propagates the exception (the existing do_GET try/except already turns this into {ok:false}).
The cache file never exceeds SEARCH_CACHE_MAX entries; the most-recently-used entries survive eviction.

items.spec: assets/a11y.js, loaded last so it decorates finished UI rather than being threaded through 19 render functions. Tabs become role=tab in a role=tablist with aria-controls/aria-selected and a roving tabindex (exactly one tab in the tab order); Arrow/Home/End move between them and switch view. Views become role=tabpanel, aria-labelledby their tab, aria-hidden when inactive. switchView is wrapped (revamp.js already wraps it once; layering is fine) to keep ARIA in sync and announce the new view through a polite live region. Modals are built by innerHTML into #modalRoot from a dozen call sites, so a MutationObserver gives every one of them role=dialog/aria-modal, aria-labelledby its heading, an initial focus on the close button, a Tab focus trap, Escape-to-close and focus restore — with no edits to any of those call sites. revamp.css adds .sr-only, a .skip-link, :focus-visible rings on every interactive surface (not just .btn/.tab), and a prefers-reduced-motion block that kills the Den's auto-spin and smooth scrolling.
items.ux: Tab from the top: a skip link, then the tab strip as one stop with arrows to move between sections. Escape closes any modal and focus returns where it was. Reduced-motion is respected.
acceptance: #tabs has role=tablist; every .tab has role=tab, aria-controls and aria-selected.
Exactly one tab has tabindex=0 at any time; the rest are -1.
ArrowRight on a focused tab moves focus and switches the view.
Every .view has role=tabpanel; inactive ones carry aria-hidden=true.
An open modal has role=dialog and aria-modal=true and takes focus; Escape closes it.
A .skip-link is the first focusable element in the document.
items.verify: scratchpad/verify-ship.js — walks the tablist contract, drives ArrowRight/Home/End, opens a card modal and asserts dialog semantics plus Escape-to-close, and checks the skip link is first in tab order.
items.notes: Ship improvement #3 ✅ 2026-08-01. Both stores check this on review, and 19 unlabelled buttons in a row was the single worst thing about using the app without a mouse.

items.title: VR: stereoscopic Den for a phone headset
items.spec: const VR = { on, ipd: 34 } in revamp.js. denVrEnter() wraps #den-world in .den-eye-l and inserts a deep clone into .den-eye-r; every id is stripped from the clone so no $('#…') lookup can resolve to scenery, and it is aria-hidden. denApply() gains a translateX(±ipd/2) prefix per eye — that lateral camera offset is the whole stereo effect. denVrToggle() requests fullscreen and starts the existing denGyroStart() head tracking on the same user gesture, because iOS requires the DeviceOrientation permission prompt to originate from one. renderDen() resets VR.on (a re-render destroys the eye wrappers) and onfullscreenchange tears stereo down when fullscreen leaves by any route. CSS: .den-vr is a two-column flex, each .den-eye carries its own perspective, and the viewport-spanning vignette and HUD are hidden so they can't straddle the seam.
items.ux: 🥽 VR in the Den toolbar splits the room into a stereo pair and goes fullscreen. Drop the phone into any Cardboard-style holder and look around.
acceptance: 🥽 VR is in the Den toolbar and toggles .den-vr on the viewport.
In VR the viewport holds exactly two .den-eye children, each containing one world.
The right-eye clone carries no id attributes anywhere in its subtree.
The two worlds' transforms differ only by the ±ipd/2 translateX prefix.
Exiting VR restores a single #den-world as a direct child of the viewport, with no leftover .den-eye.
Re-rendering the Den while in VR leaves VR.on false rather than stranding the flag.
items.verify: scratchpad/verify-ship.js — enters VR, asserts the two-eye structure and that the clone is id-free, compares the two transform strings, exits and asserts the DOM is restored, then re-renders and asserts the flag cleared.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-01. Deliberately NOT WebXR: the Den is CSS-3D, so navigator.xr would mean rewriting the room in three.js and bundling a renderer. Cardboard-style stereo works today with hardware people already own, and reuses the gyro tracking that was already there. Labelled 'Cardboard-style' in the UI rather than 'VR headset support' so it doesn't over-promise Quest/Vision Pro.

items.title: Release integrity: checksums + Gatekeeper opener on every build
items.spec: build-dmg.yml gains a checksum step (shasum -a 256 over the dmg and source zip, basenames only) and publishes SHA256SUMS.txt and OPEN-ANYWAY.command alongside them, with release notes carrying the Gatekeeper steps, a 'shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt' line and the dmg's own hash. Also adds a ship_build dispatch input, and — the real fix — the build-profile step now MERGES into data/build-flags.json instead of overwriting it. It previously wrote a fresh {"publicArt": true} object, which silently dropped shipBuild, so a public-art dispatch would have shipped the Emerald Lab into a store build.
items.ux: The dmg-latest release now carries the same four assets chest-latest does, and the notes tell you how to verify what you downloaded.
acceptance: The workflow YAML parses and exposes both public_art and ship_build inputs.
A completed run publishes dmg, source zip, SHA256SUMS.txt and OPEN-ANYWAY.command to dmg-latest.
The release notes contain the dmg's sha256 and the verification command.
Dispatching with public_art=true leaves any pre-existing shipBuild value intact.
items.verify: python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/build-dmg.yml"))' plus a real CI run; confirm the four assets and compare the published digest against the notes.
items.notes: Ship improvement #2 ✅ 2026-08-01. An unsigned download that users are told to right-click past Gatekeeper is exactly the download that most needs a checksum. The build-flags overwrite bug was found while editing this file, not reported.

items.title: App Store submission pack (privacy manifest + listing copy)
items.spec: src-tauri/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy — required for App Store submission since spring 2024; a build without one is rejected before review. Declares NSPrivacyTracking false, empty tracking domains, empty NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes (nothing is transmitted, so nothing is collected), and required-reason declarations for FileTimestamp C617.1, UserDefaults CA92.1 and DiskSpace E174.1. STORE-LISTING.md carries the names/IDs table, promotional text, full description, keywords, the App Privacy questionnaire answers, the App Review notes explaining the loopback server and the opt-in LAN mode, the screenshot shot-list, and a pre-submission checklist.
items.ux: Not user-facing — this is the paperwork that makes a submission possible.
acceptance: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is valid plist XML and parses with plistlib.
It declares no tracking and no collected data types.
STORE-LISTING.md exists with description, keywords, review notes and a checklist.
No listing string contains 'Pokémon' — every app-name slot is the <APP> placeholder.
items.verify: python3 -c 'import plistlib; plistlib.load(open("src-tauri/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy","rb"))' and grep the listing for banned strings.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-01 for the artefacts. PARTIAL, not shipped, and it stays partial until three things Brandon owns are done: the ship name is chosen (every listing string is still <APP>), a paid Apple Developer Program membership exists, and the bundled Python server is either sandboxed or the app ships direct-notarized outside the store instead. See ROADMAP-TO-PUBLISH.md §4.

items.title: Pocket Edition — the collection as one AirDrop-able file
items.spec: scripts/build_pocket.py (pre-existing, shipped in v2.2.0) inlines the collection, Game Plan, PSA-10 estimates and tap-to-open comp links into one self-contained file, with the app icon as a base64 data: URI so it works with no network. Three bottom tabs: Game Plan / Collection / Sell. server.py's build_pocket() runs it on POST /api/pocket and after every data refresh; the file is served from the writable HOME because the bundle is read-only. THIS PASS fixed three real defects rather than adding features: (1) the image fallback interpolated a double-quoted placeholder into an onerror="..." attribute, which closed the attribute early and left broken JS — every card image that failed to load threw 'Invalid or unexpected token', which offline is every single one; it is now a capturing error listener instead. (2) The Admin 'Open Pocket Edition' link still pointed at the pre-rename 'Pokémon Chest — Pocket.html' and 404'd against POCKET_NAME. (3) The Pocket header and iOS home-screen title still read 'Chest'. Also added /api/pocket to the loopback-only gate list — it runs a subprocess and a LAN peer could previously trigger it.
items.ux: Admin → iPhone Pocket Edition → Regenerate, or Scanner → Phone mode → 📦 Build Pocket file. AirDrop the file to the phone, open in Safari, Add to Home Screen.
acceptance: Opens from file:// with the browser fully offline and renders all cards with ZERO page errors.
Header and apple-mobile-web-app-title read 'Den', not 'Chest'.
The app icon is an inlined data: URI so it survives with no network.
All three bottom tabs are hit-testable at their centres and content clears the fixed bar.
Search narrows the collection list.
Tapping a card reveals its comp links (eBay raw/graded, TCGplayer, PriceCharting, FB); none render before the tap.
No horizontal overflow at 390px; no external stylesheet or script.
POST /api/pocket is refused (403) from a non-loopback peer.
items.verify: scratchpad/verify-pocket.js — 18 checks in an offline iPhone-14 context over file://. Gate checked with a spoofed Host header against the live server.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-12 (bug-fix + hardening pass; the feature itself shipped in v2.2.0). Complements the PWA rather than replacing it: the PWA needs the Mac awake on the same Wi-Fi because server.py serves it, whereas Pocket is just a file you AirDrop. Read-only on purpose — making it writable would create a second source of truth to reconcile. 1.8 MB for 1,291 cards, most of it the inlined icon and the precomputed comp URLs.

items.title: Unified product line — Den + Chest as one app (DenZ)
items.spec: The repo had forked into two shipping lines: Den 2.4.0 (19 tabs, Sets, Trade, alerts, per-card history, PWA, a11y, VR) publishing to dmg-latest, and Chest 1.16.0 (Today board, multi-game, Plinko, buy/watch, tab overflow) publishing to chest-latest. Each had features the other lacked. A plain `git merge` was NOT viable: the Chest lineage had dropped the Den features relative to the merge base, so git read them as deletions and silently removed 23 functions from app.js and 26 from server.py behind a single version-line conflict. app.js and server.py were therefore rebuilt from the Den side and the Chest additions spliced in, together with the 4 module-level declarations those functions close over (GAME_META, LS_BUYS, LS_DATA_TOUCH, _tabMoreDocWired) — omitting those threw at boot and replaced the whole app with the error panel. renderArcade was replaced wholesale by the Chest version, being a strict evolution. The tab strip became Chest's 9 primary + 10-item overflow menu. dmg-latest is now the single release.
items.ux: One app. Today board and multi-game from the Chest line; Sets, Trade, alerts, history, PWA, VR from the Den line; every view reachable from a 9-tab strip plus a More menu.
acceptance: assets/app.js contains every function from BOTH lineages (assert missing == none in both directions).
server.py contains every def from the Den lineage and Chest's codex surfaces.
App boots with no error panel and zero page errors across all 19 tabs.
Chest features live: vault hero, next steps, game bars (detects 5 games), Plinko board, overflow menu with 10 entries.
Den features live: price alerts, per-card history, snapKey, error log, qty adjust, ship/publicArt flags, About, first-run, Sets, Trade, VR.
No storage key or bundle identifier changed.
items.verify: scratchpad/verify-unified.js (27 checks) + verify-ship.js (38) + verify-trade.js (21), all green 2026-08-12.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-12. The coverage assertion over both lineages is the load-bearing part of this — the silent-deletion failure mode produced only one visible conflict and would otherwise have shipped. Keep that assertion in any future cross-line merge.

items.title: Ship name applied — Pokémon DenZ / DenZ
items.spec: bash scripts/rename.sh "Pokémon DenZ" across 16 files; tauri productName kept ASCII ("Pokemon DenZ") because it becomes the .app and .dmg filename. Store-facing name is DenZ with no "Pokémon" in it. Two real bugs in the rename tool were fixed doing this: (1) it could not see percent-encoded names, so the Admin "Open Pocket Edition" href kept 404-ing after every rename — it now rewrites the encoded form too; (2) it was not idempotent when the new name CONTAINS the old ("Den" -> "DenZ" produced DenZZ, then DenZZZ), despite its header claiming idempotence — existing occurrences are now parked behind a sentinel during replacement.
items.ux: App, window, DMG, launchers and docs all read Pokémon DenZ. Store listings read DenZ.
acceptance: No 'Pokemon Den' / 'Pokémon Den' literal remains outside the strategy docs.
A second rename run reports 0 files changed (idempotent).
POCKET_NAME in server.py and the percent-encoded href in app.js resolve to the same URL.
Storage keys (pokechest.*), bundle id and env vars are unchanged.
items.verify: Run rename.sh twice and assert 0 files changed on the second; compare quote(POCKET_NAME) against the app.js href; grep for internal ids.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-12. Brandon chose DenZ. Working build keeps the Pokémon prefix; anything store-facing must not — see BUSINESS-WARGAME.md §1.

items.title: Business wargame — SEO, pricing, launch, marketing
items.spec: BUSINESS-WARGAME.md: positioning (sells decisions, not prices; local-first as the structural moat), a competitor read against Collectr/CollX/PriceCharting/Dex/PullVault/Slabfy with the honest weakness stated (desktop-first in a mobile-first hobby), a two-tier SEO plan (high-intent calculator pages, then 395 set pages generated from the bundled codex), pricing (one-time $29 direct-first, with the reasoning for rejecting subscription and freemium), revenue scenarios at 100/1k/5k units, a pre-launch test plan that validates demand before any build, a 6-phase launch sequence gated on real blockers, and a named risk list (IP exposure on paid fan tools, PriceCharting terms, Apple review on the bundled server, the mobile gap, single maintainer).
items.ux: Not user-facing — the plan behind shipping.
acceptance: Names a specific price with reasoning, not a range.
SEO plan is buildable from data already in the repo (the codex).
Launch phases are gated on real blockers, not dates.
Risks are stated as decisions with mitigations, including the IP exposure of charging for a fan tool.
items.verify: Editorial — read it and argue with it.
items.notes: ✅ 2026-08-12. Headline: $29 one-time, sold direct first (5% fees) with the Mac App Store as discovery (30%), discovered through grading-calculator SEO and the 3D Den on video. The riskiest untested assumption is demand, not code — §5 tests it before any further build.
